-- =============================================================================
-- Lextr Semantic Layer — INCREMENTAL DDL  v2.3.0 -> v2.11.0
-- For a build that already applied the v2.3.0 baseline (16 tables).
-- Apply IN ORDER, as additive Flyway migrations. Never edit a landed migration.
--
-- Adds 23 tables and 27 columns on meta.attribute_catalog.
-- PROPOSED sections are marked and must NOT be applied without owner approval:
--   · meta.logical_hierarchy / logical_hierarchy_level   (LP-42, migration V9)
--   · attribute promotion provenance columns             (LP-44, migration V16)
-- =============================================================================

-- ---- extensions ----
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- ---- new tables ----

-- meta.attribute_pairing_catalog
CREATE TABLE meta.attribute_pairing_catalog (
    id                              bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    pairing_cd                      varchar(80)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    pairing_nm                      varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    schema_cd                       varchar(30)  NOT NULL,
    object_cd                       varchar(50)  NOT NULL,
    display_attribute_cd            varchar(32)  NOT NULL,        -- what the user sees/filters on
    filter_attribute_cd             varchar(32)  NOT NULL,        -- what SQL actually uses (indexed)
    pairing_type_cd                 varchar(30)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'LABEL_TO_KEY',
    lookup_strategy_cd              varchar(30)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CACHED_LOOKUP',
    lookup_inline_map_jsonb         jsonb,                        -- INLINE_MAP: {display:filter}
    lookup_sql_template_txt         text,                         -- RUNTIME_QUERY template
    lookup_cache_enabled_flg        boolean      NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    lookup_cache_ttl_seconds_nbr    integer      NOT NULL DEFAULT 3600,
    cardinality_cd                  varchar(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ONE_TO_ONE',
    is_bidirectional_flg            boolean      NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    is_cross_engine_flg             boolean      NOT NULL DEFAULT false,  -- POL-CE-002 gate
    filter_attribute_indexed_flg    boolean      NOT NULL DEFAULT true,   -- activation gate
    filter_attribute_index_type_cd  varchar(20),
    performance_gain_pct_est_nbr    integer,
    ai_context_txt                  text,
    client_id                       varchar(40),                  -- NULL = GLOBAL
    lifecycle_status_cd             varchar(30)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DRAFT',
    governance_review_status_cd     varchar(30)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    version_nbr                     integer      NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    created_ts                      timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_by                      varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user,
    updated_ts                      timestamptz,
    updated_by                      varchar(100),
    CONSTRAINT uq_apc_object_pair UNIQUE (schema_cd, object_cd,
                                          display_attribute_cd, filter_attribute_cd),
    CONSTRAINT fk_apc_object FOREIGN KEY (schema_cd, object_cd)
        REFERENCES meta.object_catalog (schema_cd, object_cd),
    CONSTRAINT ck_apc_type CHECK (pairing_type_cd IN
        ('LABEL_TO_KEY','NAME_TO_CODE','DESCRIPTION_TO_ID','DISPLAY_TO_FILTER')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_apc_strategy CHECK (lookup_strategy_cd IN
        ('CACHED_LOOKUP','INLINE_MAP','RUNTIME_QUERY')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_apc_cardinality CHECK (cardinality_cd IN
        ('ONE_TO_ONE','MANY_TO_ONE','ONE_TO_MANY')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_apc_diff_attrs CHECK (display_attribute_cd <> filter_attribute_cd),
    CONSTRAINT ck_apc_lifecycle CHECK (lifecycle_status_cd IN
        ('DRAFT','REVIEW','APPROVED','ACTIVE','DEPRECATED','RETIRED'))
    -- [ASSUMED-6] The "filter attribute must be indexed" activation gate is enforced in the
    --             service layer (checks pg_indexes), NOT as a DB constraint, consistent with
    --             logic-in-service. Confirm with Standards Doc (P-12).
);

-- meta.attribute_pairing_value_cache
CREATE TABLE meta.attribute_pairing_value_cache (
    id                  bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    pairing_cd          varchar(80)  NOT NULL
        REFERENCES meta.attribute_pairing_catalog (pairing_cd) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    client_id           varchar(40)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GLOBAL',
    display_value_txt   varchar(500) NOT NULL,
    filter_value_txt    varchar(500) NOT NULL,    -- ONE_TO_MANY: JSON array -> SQL IN (...)
    is_one_to_many_flg  boolean      NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    hit_count_nbr       bigint       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_hit_ts         timestamptz,
    cached_ts           timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_ts          timestamptz,
    CONSTRAINT uq_apvc UNIQUE (pairing_cd, display_value_txt, client_id)
);

-- meta.dq_rule_catalog
CREATE TABLE meta.dq_rule_catalog (
    id                      bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    dq_rule_cd              varchar(20)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,          -- DQR-####
    schema_cd               varchar(30)  NOT NULL,
    object_cd               varchar(50)  NOT NULL,
    primary_attribute_cd    varchar(32),
    rule_scope_cd           varchar(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ATTRIBUTE',
    dq_dimension_cd         varchar(20)  NOT NULL,
    threshold_txt           varchar(40),
    plain_english_txt       text         NOT NULL,
    condition_json          jsonb,
    rule_status_cd          varchar(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'REQUESTED',
    origin_cd               varchar(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'REQUESTED',
    justification_txt       text,
    last_run_ts             timestamptz,
    last_result_txt         varchar(60),
    client_id               varchar(40),                          -- NULL = GLOBAL
    created_ts              timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_by              varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user,
    updated_ts              timestamptz,
    updated_by              varchar(100),
    CONSTRAINT ck_dqr_scope CHECK (rule_scope_cd IN ('ATTRIBUTE','CROSS_ATTRIBUTE','CONDITIONAL')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_dqr_dim   CHECK (dq_dimension_cd IN
        ('Completeness','Validity','Conformity','Consistency','Uniqueness','Timeliness')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_dqr_status CHECK (rule_status_cd IN ('REQUESTED','AUTHORING','ACTIVE','RETIRED')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_dqr_origin CHECK (origin_cd IN ('REQUESTED','AUTHORED'))
    -- [ASSUMED] Accuracy is externally attested and is NOT a rule dimension. Confirm.
);

-- meta.dq_rule_attribute
CREATE TABLE meta.dq_rule_attribute (              -- cross-attribute / conditional membership
    id                  bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    dq_rule_cd          varchar(20)  NOT NULL
        REFERENCES meta.dq_rule_catalog (dq_rule_cd) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    attribute_cd        varchar(32)  NOT NULL,
    role_cd             varchar(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INVOLVED',  -- PRIMARY|INVOLVED|IF|THEN
    created_ts          timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_by          varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user,
    CONSTRAINT uq_dqra UNIQUE (dq_rule_cd, attribute_cd, role_cd)
);

-- meta.dq_result
CREATE TABLE meta.dq_result (                      -- external engine verdict ingest (append-only)
    id                  bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    dq_rule_cd          varchar(20)  NOT NULL
        REFERENCES meta.dq_rule_catalog (dq_rule_cd) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    client_id           varchar(40),
    result_cd           varchar(10)  NOT NULL,                     -- PASS|WARN|FAIL
    value_pct_nbr       numeric(6,3),
    run_ts              timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    detail_txt          text,
    CONSTRAINT ck_dqres CHECK (result_cd IN ('PASS','WARN','FAIL'))
);

-- meta.profiling_result
CREATE TABLE meta.profiling_result (
    id                  bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    schema_cd           varchar(30)  NOT NULL,
    object_cd           varchar(50)  NOT NULL,
    attribute_cd        varchar(32)  NOT NULL,
    null_pct_nbr        numeric(5,2),
    distinct_pct_nbr    numeric(5,2),
    attribute_role_cd   varchar(30),
    profile_status_cd   varchar(20),
    client_id           varchar(40),
    last_profiled_ts    timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_ts          timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_by          varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user
);

-- meta.observability_signal
CREATE TABLE meta.observability_signal (
    id                  bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    schema_cd           varchar(30)  NOT NULL,
    object_cd           varchar(50)  NOT NULL,
    signal_type_cd      varchar(30)  NOT NULL,    -- Freshness|Volume|Schema drift|Null-rate spike|Distribution shift
    severity_cd         varchar(10)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INFO',
    detail_txt          text,
    signal_status_cd    varchar(12)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'OPEN',
    client_id           varchar(40),
    detected_ts         timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_ts          timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_by          varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user,
    updated_ts          timestamptz,
    updated_by          varchar(100),
    CONSTRAINT ck_obs_sev CHECK (severity_cd IN ('HIGH','WARN','INFO')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_obs_status CHECK (signal_status_cd IN ('OPEN','TRIAGE','ACK','RESOLVED'))
);

-- meta.consumption_layer
CREATE TABLE meta.consumption_layer (
    id                      bigserial    PRIMARY KEY,
    layer_cd                varchar(40)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    layer_nm                varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    layer_kind_cd           varchar(30)  NOT NULL,   -- INTERACTIVE_QUERY|BATCH_DATASET|AI_DESCRIPTOR|REPORT_CELLS

Data access is enforced at the shared Keycloak(OIDC)+OPA gateway in front of every endpoint, so the same rules apply to analysts, rules, reports, and AI. Two policies run on every request: POL-AC-001 ring-fences access (deny-by-default; tenant/client isolation; role/purpose-based authorization; need-to-know), and POL-DC-001 applies each object/attribute's data classification (Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted, plus PII, MNPI, CSI, CDE, jurisdiction) to mask, restrict, or deny, and to gate AI exposure (ALLOWED/RESTRICTED/BLOCKED). Classification is captured at registration and is a governed property, not discretionary. This is the control set that lets model inputs satisfy MRM (SR 11-7 / OCC 2011-12) and firm-wide BCBS 239 expectations. Policies are externalized (configurable, never in code) and every access decision is logged.

points.sequencing_rationale: Domains back coded attributes; depends on attribute capture/exposure.
points.background:
[NEW IN v2.11.0 — this logic point did not exist in v2.3.0. Build from scratch.]

A coded attribute's valid values are a governed codeset (code+description), not UI mock. This point registers/reads governed domains (domain_catalog + domain_value; source INLINE|ENUMERATED|REFERENCE_TABLE) and exposes a governed AI resolve so consumers and Lexie ground on the certified, tenant-scoped, current allowed values — the critical grounding piece for Vertical AI.

POST /semantic/resolve-domain (attribute or domain_cd, tenant, as-of date) -> ACTIVE allowed values with description + AI context; policy-gated (POL-DM-001); every resolve audited. Catalog (LP-16) and Register (LP-17) consume this — no client-side value maps. DETERMINISTIC PHRASE RESOLUTION (ASK 1-8): resolve a normalised phrase (lower/trim/collapse-space, EXACT compare only — NO fuzzy/stemming/embedding/nearest) against code, description or ACTIVE synonym. Outcome is a closed set of three: EXACT (one match + resolution_basis), AMBIGUOUS (>1 match -> ALL candidates, never a best guess), UNRESOLVED (0 matches -> domain cardinality + search handle). resolution_basis (CODE|DESCRIPTION|SYNONYM|SOURCE_MAPPING + matched text) is REQUIRED on every resolved value, for the evidence trail. Return per value: value_cd, value_desc, ai_context_txt, lifecycle_status_cd, effective dates, and domain_catalog.version_nbr. Synonyms live in meta.domain_value_synonym (governed vocabulary; tenant rows may override GLOBAL as a tracked exception, override_global_flg; resolution considers GLOBAL + caller tenant, TENANT wins). Source codes map via meta.domain_value_source_map (resolution_basis=SOURCE_MAPPING). Scale: value_count_nbr on domain_catalog (service-maintained); GET /domains/{domain_cd}/values?q=&limit=&cursor= (prefix/substring, paginated, trigram-indexed); above DOMAIN_MAX_ENUMERATE_CARDINALITY the full-set resolve REFUSES (policy) and directs to search. Versioning: version_nbr bumped in-service on any value/synonym/mapping change; as_of resolves at the past version so a saved report re-explains as at its authoring date. Per-value ai_exposure_cd (inherits attribute, never wider). YN_FLAG removed — booleans are two-value ENUM_LIST. LOCALE: description + ai_context resolve in the caller's locale via meta.domain_value_text (locale -> en-US -> domain_value.value_desc fallback); value_cd is never translated. Normalisation for deterministic match is UNICODE CASE-FOLDING with a declared normalisation form (NFC + full case-fold + trim + collapse whitespace), done in-service — never SQL LOWER() (which is wrong for Turkish i, German ss, and accents). TTL: a 'latest' resolve may be cached up to DOMAIN_RESOLVE_TTL_SECONDS; a resolve pinned to version_nbr/as_of is immutable and cacheable indefinitely.

points.background:

Lextr Intelligence UC10 lets an analyst derive a report-local attribute (a maturity band, a utilisation ratio) grounded on SL attributes only. PROMOTION is the moment that working definition becomes shared meaning in the catalog — the SL's invariant. Until the rulings below are confirmed and Core supplies the workflow stages, the promotion control stays ABSENT rather than approximated.
points.scope: Additive V16 provenance on attribute_catalog (attr_origin_cd SOURCE_DERIVED|PROMOTED_DERIVED, promoted_from_report_id, derivation_expression_txt, expression_author_cd incl. consumer_traversal.purpose: How a downstream consumer (e.g. Lextr Intelligence / Lexie) starts at base objects and traverses down to learn, per attribute, whether it carries DOMAIN VALUES (enumeration), LINKS to a reference domain (a value set), LINKS to another OBJECT (a relationship/foreign key), or is a plain attribute — and which endpoint resolves each.
consumer_traversal.start: meta.object_catalog is the set of base objects. GET /objects (list) then GET /objects/{schema}/{object} returns the object with its attrs[].

per_attribute_classification.meaning: free value or measure; no controlled set and no object link
small fixed value set stored ON the attribute (incl. former booleans, now two-value ENUM_LIST)

per_attribute_classification.detect: domain_mode_cd = REF_DOMAIN and domain_cd is set
per_attribute_classification.meaning: link to a governed shared codeset in the domain store

per_attribute_classification.detect: domain_mode_cd = REF_DOMAIN and domain_ref_table_nm is set
per_attribute_classification.meaning: link projects the rows of a reference table (code/desc columns)

per_attribute_classification.detect: fk_flg = true, and/or the attribute appears in meta.semantic_relationship_catalog as a parent/child attribute
per_attribute_classification.meaning: this attribute links a ROW to another OBJECT (a join) — it does NOT define a value set
per_attribute_classification.resolve: GET /relationships?object={schema.object} -> parent/child object + attribute, cardinality_cd, join_type_cd

consumer_traversal.disambiguation: DOMAIN (enumeration or reference-domain) answers 'what values are VALID for this attribute'. OBJECT LINK (fk_flg / semantic_relationship_catalog) answers 'which other OBJECT does this attribute join to'. They are ORTHOGONAL: an attribute can be both a coded domain AND a foreign key (e.g. account_cd is a REF_DOMAIN value set AND joins to a GL-account object). Read domain_mode_cd to classify the value set; read fk_flg + semantic_relationship_catalog to classify the object link.
traversal_order: 1. GET /objects — enumerate the BOUNDED governed set (inventory): exposed + approved objects for the tenant/workspace. This reaches independent reference objects too.
2. Classify each object by role (BASE / REFERENCE / DOMAIN-BACKING).
3. GET /objects/{schema}/{object} — attrs[] with domain_mode_cd, domain_cd, domain_values_jsonb, domain_ref_*, fk_flg, semantic_role_cd, ai_exposed_flg, data_classification_cd.
5. ENUM_LIST / REF_DOMAIN attrs -> POST /semantic/resolve-domain (tenant + as-of) -> current ACTIVE allowed values.
6. fk / linked attrs -> GET /relationships?object= -> target object + attribute; recurse to step 3 (target must already be IN scope).
7. Independent reference objects: no inbound link — reason over them directly from the inventory, not via traversal.

source_tables.attributes: meta.attribute_catalog (domain_mode_cd, domain_cd, domain_values_jsonb, domain_ref_table_nm/code_col/desc_col, fk_flg, semantic_role_cd)

entry_points.name: Inventory (start here)
entry_points.reaches: every registered object, including independent reference objects
entry_points.how: GET /objects — the flat governed set, filtered by tenant + exposure/approval flags

entry_points.name: Traversal (enrich only)
entry_points.reaches: only the connected structure — objects reachable by following domain + relationship links
entry_points.how: from a base object, follow each attribute's domain / relationship links (per_attribute_classification)

object_roles.meaning: primary grain-bearing business objects; the natural roots for traversal
object_roles.detect: object_role_cd = BASE (if present), else: has a grain and inbound/outbound relationships

object_roles.meaning: standalone lookup/reference objects (currency, country, calendar); often not referred to by any attribute — reachable ONLY via the inventory
object_roles.detect: object_role_cd = REFERENCE (if present), else: no inbound relationship AND not named by any attribute domain_ref_table_nm

object_roles.meaning: reference tables that back REF_DOMAIN (table-backed) attributes
object_roles.detect: named by an attribute domain_ref_table_nm or a domain_catalog.ref_table_nm

consumer_traversal.independent_reference_note: Some reference objects are INDEPENDENT — nothing links to them via any attribute domain or foreign key — so a link-following traversal never reaches them. They are still first-class registered objects and MUST be entered via the inventory (GET /objects), classified by object role — not discovered by traversal. Treat 'unreferenced' as a normal, expected state for reference objects.

bounded_scope.principle: Bounded, not autonomous: an agent reasons within an EXPLICIT governed set, enumerated once from the inventory. It does not autonomously crawl or discover new authority.
bounded_scope.scope_set: The agent's world = registered objects where semantic_layer_enabled_flg = true AND ai_approved_flg = true AND ai_governance_cd allows AI, with attributes filtered by ai_exposed_flg, scoped by tenant (client_id) and — if used — a Tenant Workspace (LP-41). Independent reference objects are IN scope when they meet these flags, regardless of whether anything links to them.
bounded_scope.note: Traversal ENRICHES objects already in scope (resolves domains, follows links); it never expands the boundary. Anything outside the exposed/approved/workspace set is invisible to the agent by construction — that is the bound.

consumer_traversal.optional_schema: Optional (owner-approval): add object_role_cd (BASE|FACT|DIMENSION|REFERENCE|DOMAIN_BACKING|BRIDGE) to meta.object_catalog for an explicit marker. Until then, object role is DERIVED as in object_roles above.
consumer_traversal.phrase_resolution_note: To resolve an analyst's PHRASE to a code, POST /semantic/resolve-domain in phrase mode: deterministic EXACT match on code/description/ACTIVE synonym -> EXACT | AMBIGUOUS (all candidates) | UNRESOLVED. The layer never guesses; ambiguity is surfaced. Booleans are two-value ENUM_LIST (YN_FLAG removed), so they carry descriptions + synonyms like any coded attribute.

disposition_model.purpose: Against the existing Lextr Core codebase, each sub-task is first RESOLVED (does Core already satisfy this contract?) then classified, honoring low-code order reuse > configuration > extension > new.

states.UNRESOLVED: Not yet checked against Core. Default. Run the Phase-0 reconciliation prompt first.
states.REUSE: Core already satisfies this sub-task's contract as-is. Wire to it; write only the conformance test that proves the manifest's tests pass. Cannot be marked complete until that test passes.
states.ADAPT: Core has an adjacent asset that needs extension/configuration to meet the contract. Generate the reconciliation (map-gap-write) prompt, not a blank build.
states.BUILD: Nothing in Core satisfies this. Generate the standard build prompt.

disposition_model.lifecycle: UNRESOLVED -> (AI reports within the build/adapt prompt: searches repo, reports findings) -> REUSE|ADAPT|BUILD -> in-progress -> conformance/tests pass -> committed
disposition_model.reuse_gate: A REUSE sub-task may be marked committed ONLY after a conformance test demonstrating the manifest's tests_must_cover pass against the existing Core asset. (This is the one remaining hard gate; discovery itself is no longer a separate blocking step.)
disposition_model.propagation_note: Downstream-only: a REUSE/ADAPT decision conforms Core to the manifest contract or flags a gap; it never rewrites the manifest, DDL, or standards to match Core.

anti_dup.purpose: The development team exposes the live Lextr Core repo and branch to the AI. The governing risk is not 'does code exist' (the AI can see it) but that the AI authors a PARALLEL implementation instead of discovering and extending what exists. Duplication is the failure mode and is prohibited.
anti_dup.discovery_first: Discovery is folded INTO the single build/adapt prompt as its first required step — the AI searches the live repo/branch and reports SEARCHED/FOUND/DECISION before writing any code. There is no separate gating step the developer must run; the prompt itself makes discovery mandatory and self-reported. The disposition (REUSE/ADAPT/BUILD) is the AI's reported finding, not a pre-gate the developer sets by hand.
session_context: repo_url (or local path the team exposes)
branch (the exact branch exposed for this session)
hard_rules: Search the exposed repo and branch BEFORE writing anything.
If an existing controller, service, DAO, method, component, OPA package, or migration already covers this sub-task, EXTEND or CALL it — never author a parallel one.
Never create a second class, endpoint, table, column, or component that overlaps an existing one.
Before creating anything new, output: (a) the search terms/paths used, (b) what was found, (c) why nothing existing fits — the explicit reuse-vs-new decision with file paths.
Confine all reads and writes to the exposed branch's conventions and structure; do not introduce a parallel structure.
Downstream-only: conform Core to the manifest contract or flag a gap; never rewrite the manifest, DDL, or standards to match Core.
anti_dup.evidence_required: Every Phase-0 output must contain SEARCHED (terms+paths), FOUND (files+what they do), and DECISION (REUSE|ADAPT|BUILD with file paths). Build/adapt may proceed only after this evidence exists.
anti_dup.workflow_note: One prompt per sub-task. Its opening section forces the AI to (1) search the branch, (2) report what exists, (3) decide REUSE/ADAPT/BUILD with evidence, (4) for shared sub-tasks report cross-product impact — and only then write code, extending existing assets rather than duplicating. REUSE still completes only after a conformance test proves the manifest's tests pass.

product_estate.note: The Semantic Layer is a SHARED/COMMON component owned by Lextr Core and consumed by all products. Every Semantic-Layer point and sub-task is layer=shared and inherits tighter shared-layer governance. Repository topology (monorepo vs multi-repo vs shared package) is OPEN (P-10); layout is not assumed.

shared.definition: Component used across products; owned by Lextr Core; consumed by all. Wider blast radius.
rules: Cross-product regression expectation: a change is validated against all consuming products.
Independent deployability is the test: a shared change must not break any product's standalone deploy or couple products together.
A shared ADAPT/BUILD must state its cross-product impact (which products consume the asset; deploy impact).
A shared REUSE must confirm the existing asset's contract is the one ALL products rely on.

product_specific.definition: Code isolated to one product; independently deployable; a change does not affect other products.
rules: Standard review; no cross-product regression requirement.

ddl_ownership.team_owns: The team owns EXECUTING this DDL — applying it via Flyway to create/update the tables, in the manner the team defines. Full transparency: the complete DDL is embedded in the LP-01 work prompt so it is copy-run ready.
ddl_ownership.guardrail: Schema DESIGN changes flow upstream (downstream-only propagation): the team builds AGAINST this schema and does not unilaterally redesign it. A needed design change is raised as a gap to the owner (Lextr Core), not silently altered — because the Semantic Layer is shared across all products.
ddl_ownership.heading: Fixed contract — build against this; the team owns executing it (apply via Flyway). Schema design changes flow upstream, not made unilaterally.

correction_feedback.purpose: A developer/reviewer correction to AI-generated code must not evaporate at session end. It feeds back at three time-scales and routes by class, so the manifest learns and the next prompt is pre-corrected.

time_scales.within_sub_task: At completion the work prompt requires the AI to emit an ADJUSTMENTS record: what was corrected, why, and a CLASS tag (IMPLEMENTATION|CONTRACT|STANDARD|DECISION).
time_scales.across_session: Prompt generation READS the session's accumulated corrections + the sub-task's adjustments[] BEFORE producing the next prompt, so a correction made on one sub-task is already applied to the next. The generator never re-issues a prompt that repeats an already-corrected mistake.
time_scales.into_manifest: Corrections persist durably in the manifest JSON (working memory) and the gate-log (audit memory), routed by class.

routing_by_class.IMPLEMENTATION: Auto-applied to the manifest JSON (pre_build_knowledge / reuse candidates / sub-task notes updated). Written to the gate-log with details; owner is notified.
routing_by_class.CONTRACT: NOT auto-applied. Written as a PROPOSAL to the owner (SME / Data Authority) and held until approved.
routing_by_class.STANDARD: NOT auto-applied. Written as a PROPOSAL and held until approved.
routing_by_class.DECISION: NOT auto-applied. Written as a PROPOSAL and held until approved.

correction_feedback.ring_fence_note: Routing preserves downstream-only propagation: a build correction can never silently rewrite the data model, standards, or a fixed decision. Only IMPLEMENTATION corrections auto-apply; the other three classes require owner approval.

homes.manifest_json: Working memory the AI reads to generate the next prompt: per sub-task adjustments[] + a session-level corrections log + a proposals list.
homes.gate_log: Audit memory + owner notification. Same correction written here too.

viewer_boundaries.notification: A viewer-only console cannot SEND notifications. It records corrections with owner_notified=true and flags proposals prominently in the CORRECTIONS view; real email/Slack notification is a backend hook, not a manifest change.
viewer_boundaries.persistence: Console correction state is in-session (like the commit board); the durable home is the manifest JSON, regenerated/committed through the normal flow.
